If you’ve ever felt overwhelmed by the sheer amount of glowing screens in front of our kids today, please know I feel it too. It’s an emotional weight, trying to navigate what feels like a minefield of digital interactions for them. We are always learning how to teach genuine online caution without making them feel constantly monitored or stressed out. Because at the end of the day, we want them exploring freely, knowing they have tools to handle themselves.

When talking about online safety with my own 2-year-old, Maya, most discussions revolve around screen time limits or nap routines! But as she gets older, so do the threats. Lately, I’ve been focusing on teaching her-and keeping myself reminded-about digital pickpockets, which are basically scams that look super convincing until they ask for something sensitive, like a pjerkword or personal info.

One type of scam I keep hearing about involves fake school portals or educational games.
